title: The Workers in the Vineyard
text:
Jesus told of a landowner who went out early in the morning to hire laborers for his vineyard. He agreed to pay them a denarius for the day, the usual daily wage, and sent them to work.

At about nine o'clock he went out again and saw others standing idle in the marketplace. He sent them into the vineyard too, promising to pay whatever was right. He did the same at noon and at three. At about five, an hour before the end of the day, he found still others standing around. When they told him no one had hired them, he sent them into the vineyard as well.

In the evening he told his manager to call the workers and pay them, beginning with the last. Those hired at five o'clock each received a full denarius. When those hired first came, they expected more. But they also received a denarius. They grumbled that the last had worked a single hour, and he had made them equal to those who had borne the burden of the day and the scorching heat.

The landowner answered one of them: "Friend, I am doing you no wrong. Did you not agree with me for a denarius? Take what belongs to you and go. Am I not allowed to do what I choose with what belongs to me? Or do you begrudge my generosity?"
lesson: Be fair first: keep every promise you made. Then you are free to be generous, and those who received exactly what they agreed to have no real grievance when others receive more.
people: A landowner, laborers hired at different hours
